As a German inclined to tradition, I prefer to use Martin Luther's renowned translation for most purposes. An American relative gifted to me at Christmas last year a beautiful 1890 edition thereof (I hear that the Amish continue to use proper German liturgically), including the Apocrypha, a dictionary, cross-references and sundry supplements, and with gold leaf at the edges of the pages; it currently occupies a privileged position atop the desk in my study. I may sometimes use the 1951 Schlachter edition as a cross-reference. Among English translations I prefer the Authorised (King James) Version; many of its archaisms have clear parallels in German that make it rather easy for me to read. I also keep an off-line parallel Gospel that uses the World English Bible, that I admit I have not elsewhere heard of.
